en: Though your people are many,
The few Kyrgyz are no falsehood,
uncertainty_note: The emphatic construction is provisional.

text: Ханым, сенин бу кылганың чын эмес.
en: My khan, what you have done is not right.
A khan’s command is an iron snare,
When you rage and stiffen in anger,
Our misery begins to boil.
Going to the truthful one and speaking truth,
uncertainty_note: Чынчыга is a provisional manuscript form.

en: Our misery has boiled over.
There is much weeping in the breast,
uncertainty_note: Final phrase is difficult and provisional.

en: Let his jester make it grand,
uncertainty_note: Highly uncertain cursive line.

en: There is a god over your rough shoe,
uncertainty_note: Literal reading is clear enough, but proverbial sense is uncertain.

en: For solid iron there is an axe,
There is deceit within your rough shoe.
uncertainty_note: Proverbial wording is provisional.

en: That wise man knew the calamity,
uncertainty_note: The noun балак is an uncertain manuscript form.

en: If you are a shallow-witted khan,
Hang it from this neck of mine,
He spoke piercingly and defended it,
uncertainty_note: Verb is provisionally read Көзөп.

en: Speaking of what he saw and knew,
One who brings them safely through,
uncertainty_note: Elliptical participial line.

en: The white-kalpak people are not an easy people,
Having Karman’s head cut off,
uncertainty_note: Name Карман is provisional.

en: I am not one who stands in your hand.
When the khan’s age comes, cry out,
uncertainty_note: Highly uncertain cursive line.

en: I am not one who stands in your hand,
Saying, “You revealed the enemy’s secret,”
This deed of yours is not manly.
You cursed him for speaking the truth,
uncertainty_note: Final verb is provisionally read каргандың.

en: If you make strife, its blow will reach you,
uncertainty_note: Highly uncertain cursive and interpretation.

en: If you rage and stiffen in anger,
You will see it brought to submission.
uncertainty_note: Verb phrase is provisional.

en: Your folly will become your affliction.
uncertainty_note: Final noun normalized as мүшкүлүң from compressed cursive.

en: Know it clearly and keep it in mind,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: The heart that was to be driven,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Will the mind comprehend it?
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: He spoke out when telling the truth,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Yourself, fine as a thread in the true secret,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Now you have troubled my sight,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: The ruling khan suffered,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: I have no guilt and no strength,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Thus spoke Zhelzhetpes,
Speaking words as a sign,
Piercing the swelling and speaking firmly,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Saying, “My champion, listen,”
When they heard this news,
The eldest of the Kalday lords,
Said, “Are his words not reasonable?”
If he rejects the mediator,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: The khan’s good order will depart,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: The khan’s backbone will break,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: If he torments the innocent,
The people’s spirit will be broken,
The people clamored and an uproar arose,
Asking, “Where is the fault in this?”
The brave soul asked,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: He questioned him like this:
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: When the envoy speaks, heed his words,
Without making trouble or strife,
Spare his spoonful of blood.
This conduct of yours will be cruelty,
Hero Tengir, sovereign,
Restrain your raging anger,
Zhelzhetpes, knower of the people,
Spare his spoonful of blood!
If you see wrongdoing among the people,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: This will become cause for outcry,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Remain without inflicting suffering,
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: You are a twin to the envoy.
uncertainty_note: Cursive reading, wording variant, or idiomatic interpretation is provisional.

en: Warrior, you are peerless and without equal,

uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

Your ancient forefather was a great khan,

en: Warrior Chyng Tengir, understand this.
The four eshens share one root,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

en: Jeljetpes who stands in your hand,
If you strike the innocent, you will not prosper,
uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

uncertainty_note: Provisional manuscript reading: ambiguous cursive letterforms, archaic vocabulary, or uncertain word division.

When the storm beats down the reeds,

A jaw that will not submit will arise,

You become a child whom anyone may command.

en: The armored men spoke day after day,
The stone-clad men spoke plainly,
The kaldais spoke, and the people spoke.
